<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. III.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|93}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=3|verse=6}}† And the Pharisees going forth, immediatly made a consultation vvith the Herodians against him hovv they might destroy him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=7}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} vvith his Disciples retired to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee and Ievvrie folovved him, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=8}}† and from Hierusalem, and from Idumæa, and beyond Iordan. And they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing the things vvhich he did, came to him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=9}}† And he spake to his Disciples that a boate might attend on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=10}}† for he healed many, so that there preased in vpon him for {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The only touching of Christs holy person, or any part of his clothes, or whatsoeuer belonged to him, did heale al diseases.}}∷ to touch him, as many as had hurtes. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}}† And the vncleane spirites, vvhen they savv him, fel dovvne vnto him: and they cryed saying, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=12}}† {{sup|‖}} Thou art the sonne of God. And he vehemently charged them that they should not disclose him.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=13}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 5, 1. 10, 1. Lu. 6, 12. 9, 1.''}}* ascending into a mountaine, he called vnto him vvhom he vvould himself: and they came to him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=14}}† And he made that {{sup|‖}} tvvelue should be vvith him, and that he might send them to preach. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=15}}† And he gaue them povver to cure infirmities, and to cast out diuels. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=16}}† And he gaue to Simon the name {{sup|‖}} Peter. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=17}}† and Iames of Zebedee, and Iohn the brother of Iames: and he called their names, ''Boanerges'', vvhich is, ''the sonnes of thunder''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=18}}† and Andrevv and Philippe, and Bartlemevv and Matthevv, and Thomas and Iames of Alphæus, and Thaddæus and Simon Cananæus, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=19}}† and Iudas Iscariote, vvho also betrayed him.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=20}}† And they come to a house: and the multitude resorteth together againe, so that they could not so much as eate bread. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=21}}† And vvhen his had heard of it, they vvent forth to lay hands on him. for they said, That he vvas become {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See here the conceite of worldly frendes, who thinke the Zeale of Religion, madnes: and therfore count them madde, that are Zelous in Gods cause and for the Catholike faith: and the more Zelous, the more mad.}}∷ mad. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=22}}† And the Scribes vvhich vvere come dovvne from Hierusalem, said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 12, 24. Luc. 11, 15.''}}* That he hath Beelzebub: and that in the prince of deuils he casteth out deuils. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=23}}† And after he had called them together, he said to them in parables, Hovv can Satan cast out Satan? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=24}}† And if a {{sup|‖}} kingdom be deuided against it self, that kingdom can not stand. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=25}}† And if a house be deuided against it self, that house can not stand. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=26}}† And if Satan be risen against him self, he is deuided, and can not stand, but hath an end. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=27}}† No body can rifle the vessel of the strong, being entred into his house, vnles he first binde the strong, and then shal he rifle his house. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=28}}† Amen I say to you, that al sinnes shal be forgiuen the sonnes of men, and the blasphemies wherevvith<noinclude>{{rh||M iij|they}}</noinclude>
